strings.name: Roger Federer
strings.role: Retired tennis player · Grand Slam champion
strings.summary: Federer shaped modern men’s tennis through versatility, a one-handed backhand and sustained excellence. He won 20 major singles titles and 103 tour singles titles while supporting children’s education. Rivalries with Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic helped expand tennis’s worldwide audience.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected milestones; competitions, affiliations and records refer to their cited dates, not an exhaustive match log.
strings.influence.rationale: His major titles, technical style, commercial reach and long career have had global influence.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Majors and world No. 1
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Won 20 major singles titles and spent 310 weeks at world No. 1.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Public contribution
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Founded his foundation in 2003 to support children’s education in southern Africa and Switzerland.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Hall of Fame induction
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Spoke at the Newport induction ceremony, reflecting on his playing career.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Competitive farewell
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Played doubles with Nadal at the Laver Cup in London to conclude his career.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Twentieth major
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Won the Australian Open, becoming the first man with 20 major singles titles.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Eighth Wimbledon title
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Set the men’s singles record with his eighth Wimbledon championship.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Davis Cup champion
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Helped Swiss teammates win their country’s first Davis Cup.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Career Grand Slam
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Won his first French Open and completed the set of four major titles.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: First world No. 1 ranking
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Reached the ATP summit and began 237 consecutive weeks there.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: First major title
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Won Wimbledon and established the Roger Federer Foundation that year.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Turned professional
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Began his professional career and won Wimbledon’s junior singles title that year.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Basel
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Grew up in Switzerland and entered structured tennis training as a youngster.
